mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior 6-month average signals stronger household demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC drops below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 6.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically reduce corporate profit margins and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC drops below 0.04 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below the prior 6-month average signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically reduces earnings expectations and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC drops below 0.04 over any 3-year window.
